tagline: Crowd-sourcing the cure while still arguing with the pharmacy.
paragraph: I came here looking for people who actually understand what Ocrevus and Kesimpta do, and what CAR-T might do next. Someone in the thread works in pharma and walked us through helper T cells and B cells like we were in a seminar; somebody else's partner had an MRI 'lit up like a Christmas tree' three years in and still can't find anyone whose case sounds like his. That's why I keep scrolling. I'm not naive about it — I know CAR-T isn't a cure, that B-cell depleters already do a lot of what it does, and that chemo conditioning, three lumbar punctures, nine months off Kesimpta, and apheresis are not things I emotionally have in me right now. A trial site forty-five minutes away still means months of screening, and at sixty-six and a half I'm already aged out of most of them. Meanwhile I'm fighting my insurance over Ocrevus, learning I can get generic Tecfidera for $20 at CostPlus, and reading about the Ocrevus financial program that might cover up to 20K. I've had this disease twenty, thirty years; the DMTs promised to stop relapses but I'm going downhill anyway. So I weigh the placebo arm, the ICANS risk, the cancer risk, the side effects I've already lived with — and I still believe this bio-engineering is the answer. I just want to know what the long-term follow-up looks like before I sign anything.
patient_concerns: Worry about getting the placebo arm and going off Kesimpta for nine months.
Frustrated that age cutoffs of 55 close most CAR-T trials to me.
Fighting insurance over Ocrevus while learning to negotiate self-pay rates.
Want to know exactly what long-term follow-up and monitoring will look like.
person_concerns: Twenty years in, I'm still going downhill despite doing everything right.
Don't emotionally have more spinal taps, chemo, and apheresis in me right now.
Hard to find people whose lesion load and aggression match my own.
Believe this could be the answer, but fear becoming the cautionary case.
